annotations.annotation_text: Page 189 opens Book 1, Chapter 7 ("Shem the Penman") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions, featuring Shem, Shaun (as Justius), ALP (Mercius). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "dream" on page 189 ("Shem the Penman"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within Joyce's devastating self-portrait as Shem the forger-artist who writes on his own skin with bodily secretions. During this Age of Gods phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 189 ("Shem the Penman"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
